verdict.rationale: Puzzle's ReadMe-hosted API reference has a live per-endpoint "Try It!" console with generated language snippets, synced from a published OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec, so the interactive reference with runnable examples exists. The big caveat is that running requests needs the caller's own credentials: API access and sandbox credentials are request-gated by email to api@puzzle.io, not self-serve. missing for 10: self-serve credentials or a keyless sandbox so examples are runnable on arrival, independent or hands-on corroboration of the Try It console, docs-linked spec discoverability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: The ReadMe-hosted API reference ships the live "Try It!" console per endpoint ("Click Try It! to start a request and see the response here!") with generated language snippets.
Executing requests needs the caller's own credentials; API access is request-gated (api@puzzle.io) per the getting-started page.
it is the sync source for the vendor's ReadMe-hosted developer reference (puzzle-api.readme.io, linked from puzzle.io's llms.txt)
